sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes a partial skeleton with neck and back vertebrae, a partial sacrum, thirteen articulated tail vertebrae, and fragments of the pelvis and ribs.
Punatitan coughlini is the sole species in this genus, representing a titanosaurian sauropod from the Late Cretaceous Ciénaga del Río Huaco Formation in La Rioja, Argentina.
Researchers suggest a possible connection between Punatitan and the contemporary Bravasaurus regarding the titanosaur egg concentration found at the Ciénaga del Río Huaco Formation site.
Phylogenetic analysis places Punatitan as a derived member of the Lithostrotia within the clade Aeolosaurini, a subclade of Rinconsauria.
Although recovered within a clade containing two Aeolosaurus species, researchers did not assign it to that genus due to doubts regarding the placement of Aeolosaurus maximus.
This animal lived between 83.6 and 66 million years ago, spanning the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages.
